text:
sophia: Observed another quick-switch issue on prod: insights panel shows metrics for the previous workspace for ~10s after switching. Happens when switching twice quickly. Repro steps: open ws-12 -> open insights -> switch to ws-34 -> open insights immediately -> values from ws-12 flash in chart header but chart body updates later.

rb: Saw this during customer demo. Not great. I grabbed network trace: GET /api/console/prefetch?scope=insights 200, payload includes `scope.workspace_id: "ws-12"` but UI used cached prefetch.

elle: Can we confirm cache key? IIRC client uses `localCache.get('console:prefetch')` (no workspace). That would explain it.

mike: Yep. Code in `ui/prefetch.ts` line ~42: `const key = 'console:prefetch'`. We intended session-level caching to speed nav, but multi-tenant means we must be careful.

ops: If we change key to include workspace we'll multiply cache entries (we have ~5k active workspaces). Need to understand memory impact on browsers (client) and CDN (edge).

elle: Alternative: keep single key but store an envelope {workspace_id, ts, payload} and validate on read: if envelope.workspace_id !== currentWorkspace => treat as miss. Cheap and quick.

rb: Quick mitigation idea: during switch show a small skeleton and prevent reading prefetch until we verify workspace_id. DevX can add a spinner + micro-banner so users don't get misleading numbers.

sophia: Agreed. Short-term plan from triage: 1) client-side guard: verify workspace id on prefetch read (today) 2) telemetry: emit `console.prefetch.mismatch` with tags (user, prev_workspace, new_workspace) so we can measure (today) 3) evaluate cache strategy (workspace-keyed vs session with validation) next sprint.

mike: I'll PR the guard and a unit test. Also add a small integration test that simulates rapid switch to ensure no stale UI.

elle: For server-side: can we add `X-Workspace-Id` header on prefetch responses so edges/CDNs can vary? That would help downstream caching. Also consider returning `prefetch.type=light` for switch events (only counters + flags) and lazily load heavy charts.

ops: Telemetry: our `console.prefetch.hit` counter is aggregated by app+env. We should tag by workspace and user to find cross-tenant hits. But beware cardinality explosion; maybe sample or rollup by workspace size.

rb: Security check: any chance of PII leak? The prefetch payload sometimes includes `last_editor.email` in small widgets. We must ensure server strips user-scoped PII when returning prefetch for other workspaces.

sophia: Good catch. Add to action items: verify server prefetch sanitizer. If we detect any user email in prefetch for different workspace, fail fast and log an alert.

mike: Added to PR: client guard + telemetry event `console.prefetch.mismatch` (incidents tag). Will link PR in a bit.

console-deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: console-ui v2.10.7 -> canary cluster in 20m :rocket:

elle: Follow-ups: @ops can we create a short-lived dashboard showing prefetch.mismatch rate and top offending endpoints? That will help catch other endpoints returning mis-scoped payloads.

ops: On it. I'll include a heatmap by endpoint and workspace. Also adding an alert if mismatch rate > 0.5% of prefetch calls in 5m.

rb: FYI: customer affected: AcmeCorp demo yesterday. We should message CS once mitigated.

sophia: Created ticket: https://go/rdw/CON-901 (prefetch workspace context race). Owners: @mike (client), @elle (server sanitization), @ops (telemetry/dashboard). Target: hotfix to canary today, prod patch tomorrow if clean.

elle: One API design question: should prefetch endpoints accept an explicit `X-Workspace-Id` header and treat request-scoped data as authoritative? That makes server enforce scoping and reduces client responsibility. Thoughts?

mike: I like server enforcement. Client validation is still useful as safety net. We'll propose server header + validation in next API review.

sophia: Thanks team. Short-term: guard + telemetry + UX banner. Long-term: API header + cache strategy review.

ops: I'll monitor canary and surface any mismatch spikes.

sophia: Ending thread - will follow up with PR links and status.
